idiom_name: goroutine-per-connection over the runtime netpoller (no user-visible handle set)
implementation_notes: Go's runtime owns the leader role: runtime.netpoll and internal/poll arm edge-triggered notifications for descriptors and park or unpark goroutines through netpollready, so a goroutine blocked in Read or Accept is resumed exactly for the handle that became ready - there is no handle set, no leadership token and no fixed pool to rotate. Goroutine-per-connection over a listener replaces the classic structure, and a bounded worker pool (a buffered channel plus N consumers) replaces it when concurrency must be capped. The classic form is only justified when a foreign event loop must be integrated through syscall.RawConn - and then the code drives its own poller rather than a pool of threads.
pitfalls: Unbounded accepts spawn unbounded goroutines; bound them with a semaphore or a fixed worker pool, or the scheduler, memory and descriptor table become the backlog.
A descriptor wrapped with os.NewFile is not put into non-blocking mode for you, so blocking reads on it are not resumable by the netpoller and occupy a thread.
Cgo calls and long syscall.RawConn loops block the OS thread and defeat the implicit demultiplexing; keep them off the hot path or re-enter the runtime.
Connection goroutines that fail before their defer is registered leak descriptors and semaphore slots - the accounting the classic pattern gets for free by owning the thread set.
